title: Ammunition Warrant Officer
raw_text:
8-890A. Military Occupational Specialty 890A--Ammunition Warrant Officer (Eff 20211001)
   a. Licensing/certification requirement. Personnel Reliability Program, AR 50-6 (if required by
the position).
   b. Prerequisites. AR 135-100 and DA PAM 601-6.
   c. MOS 890A. MOS 890A is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOSs are 89A, 89B, and
89D.
   d. Associated SQI.
        (1) 0--No special qualifications.
        (2) 8--Instructor.
        (3) P--Parachutist.
        (4) T--Transition).
        (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
   e. Associated ASI.
        (1) Refer to DA PAM 611-21 table 6-6 (listing of universal ASIs associated with all Warrant
Officer MOSs).
    f. Qualifications.
        (1) WO1/CW2 must--
               (a) Complete the Ammunition Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC).
               (b) Have correctable vision, normal color discrimination, normal hearing, and full use
of upper and lower extremities per AR 40-501.
               (c) Meet Personnel Reliability Program (PRP) requirements per AR 50-6 when
assigned to units that have required positions.
        (2) CW3 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (1).
               (b) Complete the Ordnance Warrant Officer Advanced Course (WOAC).
        (3) CW4 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (2).
               (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Intermediate Level Education (WOILE).
        (4) CW5 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (3).
               (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Senior Service Education (WOSSE).
   g. Duties.
        (1) WO1/CW2--
               (a) Directs and coordinates the implementation of the following activities: Receipt,
storage, issue, surveillance test, maintenance, modification, destruction, and demilitarization of
conventional ammunition, missile explosive components, and other explosive items at company,
battalion, and brigade level.
               (b) Investigates and reports conventional ammunition accidents, failures, or
malfunctions.
               (c) Supervises and manages Standard Army Ammunition Systems-Modernized
(SAAS-MOD) at unit level and its associated ADP equipment.
               (d) Prepares and/or reviews ammunition storage waivers.
               (e) Prepares, reviews, and/or implements firefighting procedures for conventional
ammunition, missiles and other explosive items.
               (f) Plans, reviews, and/or implements emergency destruction of ammunition, missiles,
and other explosive items.
               (g) Plans, reviews, and/or implements policies and procedures for surveillance of
chemical and biological waste materiel.
               (h) Performs the duties of accountable officer when designated per AR 735-5.
               (i) Advises commanders on the technical aspects of ammunition, missile, and other
explosive items receipt, storage, maintenance and supply.
               (j) Plans for and schedules work requirements, observes work practices, detects and
corrects unsafe and/or improper procedures and techniques.
               (k) Manages, examines, interprets, disseminates, and verifies requirements for
technical publications in the unit.
                (l) Directs ammunition receipt, storage, maintenance and supply operations in a
tactical environment.
               (m) Interprets technical data and instructs subordinates in the technical aspects of
ammunition, missile, and other explosive items receipt, storage, maintenance and supply.
               (n) Ensures ammunition quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC) procedures are
followed.
         (2) CW3--
               (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g (1).
               (b) Conducts ammunition supply studies.
               (c) Develops, implements, and monitors programs of instruction that enhance training
of other warrant officer and enlisted MOSs.
               (d) Supervises and manages SAAS-MOD at the Sustainment Level, along with
associated ADP equipment.
               (e) Analyzes and provides reports on complex ammunition malfunctions.
               (f) Advises the brigade staff and allied armies on Class V supply, including
forecasting, requisitioning, issue, transportation, security, storage, safety, accountability,
maintenance, destruction, demilitarization, and turn-in of ammunition.
         (3) CW4--
               (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g (2).
               (b) Supervises and manages SAAS-MOD at division and EAD level, along with
associated ADP equipment.
               (c) Advises Army staff and allied armies for Class V supply.
               (d) Develops concepts, conducts studies, designs organizations, and prepares
materiel requirements; tests and evaluates systems employment and organizations; and is
proficient in the Total Life Cycle Systems Management (TLCSM) model.
               (e) Provides technical and tactical assistance at any echelon of command or support
activity for the U.S. Army, or liaison activities with allied armies.
               (f) Presents written or oral briefings to line, staff, and professional personnel on
ammunition supply, maintenance and related subject matters.
       (g) Administers the MOS Life Cycle Management and oversees personnel proponent
functions affecting CMF 89 --Ordnance.
         (4) CW5--
               (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g (3).
               (b) Acts as the technical advisor to higher echelons of command and to allied armies.
               (c) Provides technical advisory services on contracting and production matters to
commanders.
               (d) Provides coordination between military and industry during development, testing
and fielding of new munitions and missile explosive components.
               (e) Manages the development of training packages to ensure Army personnel are
prepared to receive, store, maintain and supply new munitions and missile systems prior to
fielding.
               (f) Serves as Army Theater subject matter expert (SME) and advisor for all aspects of
munitions management, to include the development of command policies and procedures for
munitions management, SAAS-MOD operations, and explosive safety.
               (g) Performs other officer level duties as required consistent with senior staff officer
responsibilities.
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
         (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
         (2) A minimum OPAT score of (Standing Long Jump (LJ) - 0120 cm, seated Power Throw
(PT) - 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036 shuttles)
is required in Physical Demand Category “Moderate” (Gold).
         (3) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels:
W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are
listed in the following standards of grade tables:
               (a) Table 8-890A-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
               (b) Table 8-890A-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
